# Abstract {.unnumbered}

Velkscala 1.0 is a global gridded demographic database reconstructing population counts, age-sex pyramids, and vital flows from 10000BC to 2025AD at 5-arcminute resolution, published by Confoederatio, Research Division. Our validation framework evaluates two foundational demographic regimes: the Contemporary Demographic Transition (CDT, 1850--2019AD) against Human Mortality Database (HMD), United Nations World Population Prospects (UNWPP), and Niva et al. (Kummu) subnational vital records; and the Neolithic Demographic Transition (NDT, 10000BC--1000AD) across five independent agricultural origins and 19 subnational geocodes against Bocquet-Appel paleodemographic priors. Across the CDT benchmark, isotonic Pool-Adjacent-Violators (PAVA) and Whittaker-Henderson graduation clamped to Stadester bounds elevate geometric mean age-sex goodness-of-fit ($R^2$) from 0,4625 (raw multinomial logit) to 0,6092 (+0,1466 improvement), reaching 0,8140--0,8736 across pre-1950 historical HMD cohorts. Across the NDT domain, raster cohort buffers confirm spatially endogenous age-structure differentiation across all 19 tracked geocodes and capture both the Bocquet-Appel immature juvenile proportion surge ($p(5\text{--}19)/p(5+)$) and the European Linearbandkeramik (LBK) boom-and-bust cycle.

# Background {.unnumbered}

Continuous gridded reconstructions of historical human populations have traditionally relied on static regional growth multipliers or uniform age-structure templates [@hyde2017]. While long-run land-use series such as HYDE 3.2 provide spatially explicit estimates of total population and arable land back to 10000 BC, they do not resolve age-sex pyramids, birth and death flows, or subnational demographic regimes^[Both 0 AD and 1950 AD serve as primary structural benchmark epochs across the Velkscala 1.0 horizon: 0 AD anchors the classical imperial census domain across Eurasia, whereas 1950 AD marks the onset of harmonised United Nations World Population Prospects (UNWPP) national registration.]. Consequently, downstream paleodemographic and economic analyses have lacked a unified, empirically validated grid that couples Holocene agricultural transitions with modern vital registration.

# Methodology {.unnumbered}

### Premodern Multinomial Logit (MNL) Cohort Ensemble (10000 BC--1750 AD) {.unnumbered}

In **Velkscala 1.0**, demographic cohorts and vital flows are generated endogenously at the pixel and geocode level across two coupled regimes. Across the pre-industrial domain (10000 BC--1750 AD), a 34-covariate multinomial logit (MNL) ensemble predicts five-year age-sex bracket shares from local agricultural intensity (arable cropland, shifting cultivation, and irrigation), settlement density, and climatic envelope priors [@hyde2017].^[Unlike static regional life-table lookup schemes, the 34-covariate MNL ensemble evaluates local arable land per capita and settlement hierarchy at every 5-arcminute grid cell before aggregating to subnational and sovereign geocodes.]

### Contemporary Isotonic PAVA and Whittaker-Henderson Graduation (1750--2025 AD) {.unnumbered}

Across the rolling contemporary transition (1750--2025 AD), raw MNL cohort probabilities are graduated via isotonic Pool-Adjacent-Violators (PAVA) and Whittaker-Henderson smoothing kernels [@ayer1955; @whittaker1923], and subsequently clamped to Stadester total population bounds. This two-stage graduation enforces monotonic mortality schedules across adjacent cohorts while preserving observed urban-rural and subnational fertility differentials.

# Testing and Validation {.unnumbered}

### Contemporary Demographic Transition (CDT) Benchmark Design (1850--2019 AD) {.unnumbered}

To verify out-of-sample fidelity before post-1950 United Nations census splicing, we subject the proxy estimators to two empirical stress tests. First, we evaluate the **Contemporary Demographic Transition (CDT)** across 9 benchmark epochs (1850--2019 AD, up to $N = 189$ sovereign ISO3 jurisdictions), comparing raw MNL cohort probabilities and Stadester-clamped pyramids against empirical life tables from the Human Mortality Database (HMD) and UNWPP [@hmd2024; @unwpp2024], alongside vital birth and death stocks from Niva et al. [@niva2023].^[In the final Velkscala 1.0 production composite, proxy estimators are retired from 1950 AD onwards in favour of direct empirical UNWPP and Niva et al. subnational vital records; evaluating the uncalibrated proxy through 2019 AD provides a stringent out-of-sample stress test across heterogeneous developing-world fertility transitions.]

### Neolithic Demographic Transition (NDT) Benchmark Design (10000 BC--1000 AD) {.unnumbered}

Second, we audit the **Neolithic Demographic Transition (NDT)** from 10000 BC to 1000 AD (21 epochs) across five independent agricultural hearths and 19 national and subnational geocodes against archaeological juvenile mortality priors [@bocquet2002; @bocquet2008], alongside Holocene radiocarbon and land-use reconstructions [@shennan2013; @timpson2014; @hyde2017].

# Results {.unnumbered}

### Contemporary Demographic Transition (CDT) Empirical Fit {.unnumbered}

Across the contemporary validation horizon, graduating raw multinomial logit age-sex probabilities through isotonic PAVA and Whittaker-Henderson kernels [@ayer1955; @whittaker1923], clamped to Stadester total population bounds, substantially improves demographic fit. Across all evaluated country-epoch pairs, geometric mean $R^2$ rises from $0,4625$ under raw MNL baseline probabilities to $0,6092$ post-clamping (an overall improvement of $\Delta R^2 = +0,1466$; Figure \ref{fig:cdt-dashboard} and Table \ref{tab:cdt_age_sex}).^[Country-level $R^2$ is computed as the arithmetic mean of male and female five-year cohort fits per ISO3 jurisdiction and aggregated across jurisdictions via geometric mean.]

Crucially, within the pre-1950 historical domain where proxy models operate as the primary estimator in Velkscala 1.0 [@hmd2024], clamped age-sex $R^2$ consistently exceeds $0,81$, reaching $0,8525$ in 1850 ($N = 8$ HMD countries), $0,8505$ in 1900 ($N = 11$), $0,8736$ in 1920 ($N = 12$), and $0,8140$ in 1940 ($N = 16$). Across global vital flows (1950--2019 AD), out-of-sample births and deaths track empirical UNWPP and Niva et al. benchmarks with median country accuracy of $83,1\%$ and $78,9\%$ respectively (Table \ref{tab:cdt_vital_flows}).

### Neolithic Demographic Transition (NDT) Paleodemographic Findings {.unnumbered}

Across the **Neolithic Demographic Transition (NDT)** domain ($10000\text{ BC}$ to $1000\text{ AD}$, $21$ historical epochs; Figure \ref{fig:ndt_dashboard} and Table \ref{tab:ndt_scorecard}), our gridded cohorts reproduce the three canonical paleodemographic signatures established by Bocquet-Appel [@bocquet2002; @bocquet2008]: (1) a transient surge in maternal fertility and annualised population growth ($r$\%/yr) peaking approximately $\Delta t \approx 700\text{--}800$ years post-onset [@bocquet2002]; (2) a pronounced elevation in the immature juvenile proportion ($p(5\text{--}19)/p(5+)$), reflecting shortened interbirth intervals [@bocquet2008]; and (3) a subsequent post-boom deceleration or boom-bust contraction as agrarian density encountered ecological and epidemiological frontiers [@shennan2013; @timpson2014].

- **Unique Age Structure Per Geocode**: Direct audit of raster cohort buffers confirms that age-structure proportions are **spatially unique per geocode and per pixel**, driven by local covariates [@hyde2017] and graduated via isotonic PAVA/Whittaker algorithms [@ayer1955; @whittaker1923]. As shown in Table \ref{tab:ndt_geocodes}, at $0\text{ AD}$ under-5 shares ($p(0\text{--}4)$) range from $12,96\%$ (South Korea) to $16,22\%$ (Syria/Levant), while Bocquet-Appel juvenile ratios range from $30,15\%$ to $49,88\%$. At $600\text{ AD}$, Italy exhibits an elevated IJP ($41,66\%$) amidst population contraction ($7,50\text{M} \rightarrow 3,06\text{M}$), capturing demographic crisis dynamics associated with late antique mortality shocks.

- **The European LBK Boom-and-Bust Dynamic**: In Europe, total population expands to $1,47\text{M}$ at $6000\text{ BC}$ before contracting to $1,12\text{M}$ at $5000\text{ BC}$ ($r = -0,027\%$/yr; Table \ref{tab:ndt_trajectories}). Rather than contradicting the NDT, this trajectory reproduces the empirically established **Early Neolithic Linearbandkeramik (LBK) boom-and-bust cycle** [@shennan2013; @timpson2014], wherein early farming communities expanded rapidly across European loess soils before experiencing soil depletion and pathogen-induced crashes prior to Middle Neolithic recovery ($+0,044\%$/yr by $4000\text{ BC}$).

# Limitations {.unnumbered}

Three structural limitations govern the interpretation of our paleodemographic and contemporary proxy series. First, because infant skeletal remains ($p(0\text{--}4)$) suffer differential taphonomic loss in archaeological cemeteries [@bocquet2002; @bocquet2008], the juvenile ratio $p(5\text{--}19)/p(5+)$ serves as the primary osteological index of fertility across the Neolithic transition, led by Southeast Asia ($11,8\times$ growth elevation; $+1,42\text{ pp}$ IJP surge) and the American Southwest ($1,6\times$ elevation; $+2,79\text{ pp}$ IJP surge peaking at $\Delta t = +600$).^[Osteological cemetery assemblages systematically under-represent neonatal and infant burials due to lower bone mineral density in the $0\text{--}4$ age bracket; Bocquet-Appel's $p(5\text{--}19)/p(5+)$ ratio excludes infants to provide a taphonomically invariant proxy for crude birth rates.]

Second, between $8000\text{ BC}$ and $7000\text{ BC}$, baseline population in HYDE exhibits a step increase across Eurasia ($+0,071\%$/yr in Southwest Asia; $+0,080\%$/yr in Europe) tied to Holocene climatic amelioration [@hyde2017]. Isolating this pre-onset step confirms that post-onset agricultural expansion remains distinctly elevated above homeostatic foraging baselines ($0,01\text{--}0,03\%$/yr) [@bocquet2008; @shennan2013], while continental raster integration naturally smooths micro-site cemetery peaks ($\sim 0,8\text{--}1,1\%$/yr) to macro-regional millennial rates ($\sim 0,07\text{--}0,15\%$/yr).

Third, across the post-1950 contemporary horizon, uncalibrated proxy divergence reflects the expansion of the validation sample from historical European HMD registers ($N = 8\text{--}16$) to $N = 189$ global UNWPP jurisdictions [@hmd2024; @unwpp2024], which exhibit heterogeneous fertility transitions and subnational migration schedules [@niva2023].

# Conclusion {.unnumbered}

Taken together, our dual-regime validation demonstrates that coupling a 34-covariate premodern multinomial logit ensemble with isotonic PAVA and Whittaker-Henderson graduation [@ayer1955; @whittaker1923] yields internally consistent, spatially endogenous age-sex pyramids and vital flows across the full 12025-year Velkscala 1.0 domain. Across the Contemporary Demographic Transition, Stadester-clamped graduation elevates overall geometric mean $R^2$ by $+0,1466$ (reaching $0,8140\text{--}0,8736$ prior to 1950 AD), while across the Neolithic Demographic Transition, pixel-level cohort graduation captures both regional Bocquet-Appel juvenile surges and the European Linearbandkeramik boom-and-bust dynamic.
